extracted.intended_audience: physicians, surgeons, natural philosophers, and learned society readers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating historical medical case reports and related medico-legal findings about blood transfusion (evidence, procedure, safety, and regulatory responses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of successful prior transfusions
rubrics_metrics.description: That the operation of transfusion was twice performed upon Antony Mauroy, and that it succeeded so well those two times, that the patient was seen for two months after it in his good senses and in perfect health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a primary evidential fact considered by the court (Extract of the Sentence, point 1). Used to weigh causal connection between transfusion and subsequent death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncompliance with post-operative instructions by attendants
rubrics_metrics.description: That from the time of the two first operations his wife gave him eggs and broths, and bedded with him four times, notwithstanding the prohibition of those that treated him, and that she carried him to her house without speaking to them of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as evidence that post-operative care and instructions were not observed, bearing on cause-of-death and on whether relapse was due to transfusion or to patient/family behaviour (Extract, point 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of possible poisoning or adulteration of food
rubrics_metrics.description: That since that time, he went from one public house to another, and took tobacco, and falling ill again, his wife gave him spirituous liquors to drink, and broths, wherein she mixed certain powders; and that Mauroy having complained that she would poison him, and gave him arsenic in his broths; she hindered the assistants from tasting thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by tribunal as a concrete alternative explanation for death (poisoning), including witness accounts and the reported death of a cat after eating leftover broth (later testimony).

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic violence and hostile marital relations as relevant evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: That du Mauroy had frequent quarrels with his wife since, and that she gave him many strokes, as sick as he was, but having once received a box on the ear from him, she said he should repent it though she should die for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual evidence of motive, instability, and risk that informed the investigation and culpability assessments (Extract, point 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances and procedural failures of the third transfusion attempt
rubrics_metrics.description: That when transfusion was attempted the third time, it was at the instant request of his wife; those that were to perform the operation refusing to do it without permission of the Solicitor General; that some days after the operation was begun, scarce any blood issued either out of the foot or of the arm of the patient, a pipe was inserted, which made him cry out, though it appeared not that any blood of the calf had passed into his veins: that the operation was given over, and that the patient died the next night.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factual findings about the attempted operation used to assess causation and to judge procedural adequacy; highlights incomplete transfusion, procedural distress, and temporal proximity to death (Extract, point 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obstruction to post-mortem examination
rubrics_metrics.description: That this woman would no ways suffer any person to open the body of her husband, saying in excuse, he was already in the coffin, when he was not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as an obstructive act that prevented definitive determination of cause of death; grounds for suspicion and for ordering further inquiry/custody (Extract, point 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of solicitation/bribery to produce false accusations
rubrics_metrics.description: That a good while after the decease of the said du Mauroy, three physicians did solicit the said woman to take money, and to make complaints that the transfusion had killed her husband ... that one had offered 12 louis d'or, if he would depose that du Mauroy died in the very act of the transfusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to impeach subsequent accusations and to identify possible malicious actors attempting to blame the operators; grounds for examining and summoning alleged solicitants (Extract, point 7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to investigate fully and take further informations
rubrics_metrics.description: That the matter was important enough to inquire into the bottom of it; that there was cause enough to examine this woman. Where she had those powders? Why she had given them to her husband? And by whose order? Why she had hindered the opening of the body by a lie? That he required further information might be taken about it, and she in the mean time put in safe custody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural standard set out by the lieutenant: where reasonable cause exists, authorities should take further depositions, detain suspects, and pursue origins of incriminating facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation: transfusion on humans requires approbation of Parisian faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: That for the future no transfusion should be made upon any human body but by the approbation of the physicians of the Parisian faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A preventive regulatory requirement ordered by the court to limit practice to overseen, approved physicians; cited as the decree's principal regulatory outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement: personal appearance and examination may be demanded
rubrics_metrics.description: It was decreed that the widow of du Mauroy should on a set day appear personally, and undergo the examination upon the alleged informations; and that more ample informations should be made of the contents in the complaint of Mr. Denis; and then, that for the future no transfusion should be made ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court practice: require accused/complainant to appear for examination and collect fuller information before disposing of the case; execution of summons may be deferred if further information makes appearance unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical criterion for appropriate transfusion practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless more blood was drawn from the man than was infused into him (which does not appear to have been the case in the two first trials) a sudden and considerable plethora would be produced; a change little suited to relieve a maniacal affection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical critique: to relieve certain conditions (e.g., mania), transfusion without adequate removal of recipient blood risks producing harmful plethora; thus proper volume management is a clinical criterion for selecting and executing transfusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety standard: do not open arteries in both donor and recipient on humans
rubrics_metrics.description: Libavius proposed to open arteries in both; which indeed may be practised upon brutes, but ought by no means upon man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical safety admonition against dangerous techniques appropriate to animals but unacceptable in human practice; used to distinguish feasible animal procedures from human-ethical/practical limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and usage guidance for tubulous (tapered) spectacles
rubrics_metrics.description: Use spectacles with the largest circles, remove the glasses and put black Spanish leather taper-wise into the emptied circles (widened to take in the whole eye at the wider end); colour the leather on the inside with ink; adjust orifice width/length for print size; have tubes moveable so you may draw them longer or shorter; sometimes use one eye or the other for ease; tubes may be of paper with inner folds drawn out from one inch to three; black the inside with a non-lustrous black.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical how-to for making low-tech 'tubulous' aids for decayed sight: materials, dimensions, adjustment strategy, rationale (smaller remote orifice improves clarity), and notes on possible use of lenses for squint-eyed persons and effects on light sensitivity and preservation of sight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optical projection contrivance in a light room (Hooke)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposite to the place or wall where the apparition is to be, let a hole be made of about a foot in diameter or larger; without this hole place the picture or object inverted, and by means of looking-glasses set behind, if the picture be transparent, reflect the rays of the sun so as that they may pass through it towards the place where it is to be represented; let the picture be encompassed on every side with a board or cloth so that no rays may pass beside it; if the object be a statue or some living creature, then it must be very much enlightened, by casting the sun beams on it by refraction, reflexion, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stepwise practical instructions for producing apparent images/appearances on a wall in a well-lit room; emphasizes control of stray light, inversion of object, use of mirrors to direct sunlight, and strong illumination for opaque/3D objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sand-flood mitigation and land-reclamation techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: By stopping of it four or five years with furze hedges, set upon one another as fast as the sand levelled them, raising sand-banks near 20 yards high to bring it into the circuit of about eight or ten acres; then in one year, by laying some hundreds of loads of muck and good earth upon it, reduce it to terra firma; community assistance to remove loads and cut a passage through the main body of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical methods used at Downham to arrest migrating sands and restore buried land and buildings: progressive hedging, construction of high banks, application of topsoil/manure, and cooperative labour to remove and reclaim land.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for measuring magnetic variation via solar azimuth observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Record Sun's observed altitude, magnetical azimuth, and Sun's true azimuth; note the greatest difference (here 14 minutes) and take the mean for the true variation (concluding 1 deg. 27 min. on June 13, 1666); repeat observations to note changes (e.g., increase ~6 minutes westerly the next year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observational protocol: multiple sun-altitude/azimuth readings, compute differences, take mean as estimate of magnetic variation; use repeated measurements across years to detect secular change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical observation linking highest spring and annual tides to equinoxes
rubrics_metrics.description: From many former observations Capt. Sturmy assures, that the highest spring and annual tides there are about the equinoxes, according as the moon is near the full or change, before or after that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phenomenological rule for local tidal timing: highest tides observed around equinoxes and when moon is near full or new; useful for anticipating tidal extremes.
